page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. This server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong capabilities in specific data processing tasks. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.48 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.31 GB/sec, alongside a strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 257.74 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing ranks in the top tier with a score of 4380.5, while database operations and static web serving throughput register as strong. Standard CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core, fall into the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the integration of local NVMe SSD storage alongside dedicated ARMv9 cores offers high resource density for workloads requiring rapid local data access without the overhead of network-attached storage. The balanced memory-to-CPU ratio and strong database benchmark results make this instance suitable for database operations, static web serving, and data compression tasks. However, the lack of AVX or AMX instruction support and the absence of a GPU limit its applicability for heavy vector-based machine learning acceleration, though it maintains average performance for small-to-medium scale LLM text generation.
